the surface roughening of a laser-ablated surface is not dependent on the pulse duration of the laser used.
the surface rough- ness of the ablated propellant surface is dependent on the pulse duration, the laser scanning pattern, and the fluence.
laser ablation of metals with 10- and 500-ps laser pulse duration leads to similar surface roughness values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-term ablation of propellants in the nanoseconde to picosecond time scale.
laser ablation propulsion and the surface properties that are produced by the laser ablation process.
the minimization of thrust noise in the long-term operation of laser ablation propulsion systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surface properties of the ablation layer are determined by the laser fluence and the scanning strategy, independent of the laser pulse duration.
the surface quality is a function of the laser pulse energy density, the laser pulse duration, the scanning pattern, the number of ablation layers, the material properties, and the laser spot size.
laser ablation propulsion with 500-ps lasers is a viable option for low-noise microthruster operation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of 10- or 500-ps pulses for laser ablation propulsion is equally viable.
the surface roughening is not the dominant source of the thrust noise.
a scanning strategy with 50% overlap and 1% step size is recommended.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface properties of laser ablated materials are not significantly altered by the pulse length, and therefore laser ablation propulsion is not a pulse-length-specific technology.
the surface roughening of a laser-ablation propellant is not a significant factor for the thrust noise of a laser propulsion system.
